items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Well named, documented and gofmt-clean, with a layout comment for the wire format. The cap applies: single-letter locals carry decode logic, e.g. `p := &Polygon{...}`, `l := &Loop{...}`, `n := readCount(d, "clipped edges", maxEdge)`, `pts = pts[n:]`.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: shapeindex_encode.go is 537 lines (>500). ShapeIndex.decode is about 104 lines with 3-4 levels of nesting (>100 cap); decodeIndexShape is near that size too. It ignores the typeTag convention with a parallel shapeIndexShapeType enum, and per-shape codecs sit in one file, not next to each type.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Every count is bounded via readCount before allocating. Slices are preallocated up to decodeAllocChunk at most. A CRC-32C checksum is checked, and cell IDs, order and edge refs are validated. The target is left unchanged on error. Minor point: a catch-all recover() turns panics into errors, but it returns the error rather than swallowing it.

items.name: Existing encodings and Shape interface unchanged
items.name_zh: 既有编码格式与 Shape 接口不变
items.evidence: Only additive: two new files (shapeindex_encode.go, its test). No existing per-shape wire format, typeTag value or Shape interface method was changed.
